glossario.Chi c'è c'è, chi non c'è non c'è: Quien no se haya escondido, tiempo ha tenido

note: Spanish of Spain, informal «tú»; masculine for the player where Italian is masculine. Quotation marks follow the RAE: «» outside, “” inside, full stop after the closing quote. Menu buttons are infinitives (Continuar, Reanudar, Bajar con las botellas), as is usual in Spanish UIs; hints are imperatives. To double-check: (1) Hatch's count ends with the Spanish hide-and-seek formula «¡Quien no se haya escondido, tiempo ha tenido!» (also in his death line and on the den drawing, «QUIEN NO SE HAYA ESCONDIDO»); it is longer than the Italian, the voice speeds up to fit. (2) In the Journal, «10!» and «HOT DOG» are left as drawn in the den images (no inverted ¡). (3) Lampy's bracelet reads «KG 3,1 – julio 2003», translated from the Italian Journal text, although docs/LOCALIZZAZIONE.md says the den image now shows «3100 g – 7 / 2003»: if the Italian changes, change it here too. (4) Deliberately Spain-specific words: cubo, prismáticos, manguitos, ceras, bocadillo, tarta, tiovivo, aparato (braces), coger, almadrabas; «tiques» is the RAE spelling (many would write «tickets»). (5) Real species names are the FAO/Spanish commercial names, except: Brama brama «Castañola» (FAO «Japuta», which reads like a swear word), Sparisoma cretense «Vieja (pez loro)», Lampris guttatus «Pez luna real», Trachinus draco «Pez araña» (FAO «Escorpión»); «Granadero», «Pez víbora», «Pez linterna», «Caballito de mar» are group names, like the Italian. (6) Glitch family = «Distorsionados» (avoids the anglicism «glitcheados»); corrupt = «Corrompidos» («corruptos» suggests politicians). (7) Drawings: «¡BÚSCAME!» instead of the draft «¡ENCUÉNTRAME!» (shorter, and what a hiding child shouts); «FELIZ CUMPLEAÑOS» without ¡! like the Italian and English garland, so it is drawn bigger; «AGOSTO 97» is the same word as in Italian. (8) Flyer: «barca» instead of the draft «barco» (the game's small boat is «la barca» everywhere); «¡Sin experiencia!» means no experience needed, as elliptical as «Nessuna esperienza!». (9) A few fish names exceed 16 characters (Estornino Rebobinado and Castañuela Granulada 20, Palometón sin Señal 19), like their English counterparts; «Barracruda» equals the Italian because the pun (barracuda + cruda, raw) works the same in Spanish. (10) Least sure fish names: Pejeraspa, Desollacho, Mirainfierno, Salmonojos, Pez Gritarra.
